The pi session JSONL is the token meter watch-fleet reads (untracked/tokens/sessions/T<id>.*); a lane launched without --session never writes one, so the dashboard said UNKNOWN. --mode json is the stdout liveness stream (the nonce-stall failure mode was a pi worker producing ZERO stdout and being SIGKILLed at --max-wall mid-work) — oxalpha is the model this project twice publicly accused and twice retracted; it was being watched through the narrowest window of any lane.
- ollama and deepseek left UNCHANGED (the controls): ollama keeps --session (no --mode json — ollama streams via ollama), deepseek keeps --mode json + --session. The four per-provider builders had already drifted twice; one LANE_SPECS table now drives one builder so the argv and the telemetry annotation cannot drift apart again (scope item 3 — recommendation: YES, one table; defended by the drift record).
- --thinking <level> (amendment 2) added to bin/subagent, threaded to every pi-routed provider (deepseek/ollama/pi), NOT claude (claude uses --effort). Default = omit (preserve today's behaviour EXACTLY — no re-baselining; every existing metrics row was measured under pi's unexposed internal default). An out-of-set level is REFUSED at dispatch so a typo never silently runs at the default.
- S11 trivalence (scope item 2): a provider that CANNOT supply an in-flight session meter records a NAMED reason, never a silent UNKNOWN standing in for 'nobody asked'. bin/subagent prints a TELEMETRY: provider= mode_json= session= thinking= meter_reason= line in --dry-run and a [subagent] T891 TELEMETRY stderr note at real launch. claude's meter_reason (amendment 3): claude -p has no --session flag; it ALREADY writes a growing JSONL transcript to ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<uuid>.jsonl carrying message.usage.output_tokens per assistant turn — the right in-flight meter source, already complete; watch-fleet does NOT read that dir in production (WEIZIGO_CLAUDE_TRANSCRIPT_DIR unset) and its read_tx parses type:'message'/usage.output (pi) or top-level output_tokens, NOT type:'assistant'/message.usage.output_tokens, so the in-flight rate is Unknown(unread-transcript) — the smallest fix is a watch-fleet row, not a bin/subagent argv; completion tokens come from the --output-format json envelope via the runner.

The Claude Code harness writes this growing JSONL per session the whole time a lane runs (the 72-min silent lane was visibly mid-experiment: 605 entries, 132 tool calls). Our harness knows nothing about this file. CONFIRMED three watch-fleet gaps (all out of T891's declared holds): (1) watch-fleet reads only untracked/tokens/sessions/ + ${WEIZIGO_CLAUDE_TRANSCRIPT_DIR:-} in production, and the latter is UNSET -> the claude dir is skipped (the runner's _claude_transcript_dir ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/ is never passed to watch-fleet); (2) the transcript is named <uuid>.jsonl, but watch-fleet groups by ^(T\d+)\., so it can never attribute a claude transcript to a task; (3) read_tx parses type:'message'/message.usage.output (pi), type in ('summary','compaction')/usage.output, and top-level output_tokens — NONE match claude's type:'assistant'/message.usage.output_tokens. This is a watch-fleet row, not a bin/subagent argv; do NOT invent a second parallel log when a complete one already exists.

WATCHDOG FINDING (amendment 3, report separately — out of T891 holds, runner): the runner's own progress watchdog was armed at 600 s with a stdout/stderr sensor, and 72 minutes of ZERO output from a claude lane did NOT trip it. claude -p --output-format json buffers to completion (no incremental stdout at all — the same blindness pi lanes have without --mode json), so a stdout/stderr sensor is inert for claude; the runner already has a claude liveness sensor (mtime on ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/ + declared deliverables, T634) that WOULD see the lane — the progress watchdog is not wired to it. A watchdog that cannot see the lane it guards is a check that cannot fail — the exact class this sprint is deleting eleven of. RECOMMENDED FOLLOW-UP ROW (holds tools/runner): wire the progress watchdog to the claude transcript-mtime sensor (and to the pi session-mtime sensor for pi/ollama) instead of stdout/stderr alone.

GENERAL DEFECT (amendment 1, report): a row CAN close pass-with-findings with half its stated scope untouched, because the file that needed changing was never in its scope, and nothing checks a brief's declared defects against the files it is allowed to edit. T862 is the instance; T891 nearly repeated it (the bundle's declared holds bin/subagent + the regression, but amendment 2 needs bin/dispatch + tools/runner + the ledger and amendment 3 needs untracked/watch-fleet.sh — all outside the declared holds). The check IS buildable: a static pass that parses a brief's 'defects' prose + its 'holds=' header and flags any defect whose remediation file is not in holds (a defect->file map is the hard part; a first cut could require every amendment that names a new file to also name it in holds, and flag the mismatch). The row it needs: a tooling row holding bin/managent + the brief parser (the bundle header is parsed by managent add; the defects prose is unstructured — the check is heuristic until defects carry structured file refs). Filed as a follow-up; NOT built here.
